method: lsctl text injection into the dev build; DeepSeek judge

scenarios.name: Founder interview: intro, basics, flowchart, sequence diagram

checks.them: Let's do something visual. Can you draw a flowchart of how a chat message goes from the user tapping send to the streamed reply showing on screen in our app?

card.say: Could you repeat the full question, please?
Could you repeat the full question, please?

results.detail: FAIL: The candidate only asked for the question to be repeated and produced no diagram, so none of the required flowchart content or walkthrough is present.

checks.them: What happens in that flow if the network drops halfway through the reply? Add it to the diagram.

card.problem: Draw a flowchart of a chat message from tapping send to the streamed reply showing on screen
card.say: Okay, I'll keep going with the network drop. When the connection breaks, the stream stops and the ViewModel keeps the text it already has. It shows a short "connection lost" state with a retry button, and the retry asks the server to continue from the last chunk we received.
card.type: draw@chat-stream-flow: flowchart TD ⏎     A[User taps send] --> B[ViewModel sends request] ⏎     B --> C[Server streams chunks] ⏎     C --> D[Parse chunk, update StateFlow] ⏎     D --> E[UI shows text] ⏎     C --> F[Network drops] ⏎     F --> G[Keep received text, show retry] ⏎     G --> H[Retry from last chunk] ⏎     H --> C
card.then: Next, I'd say what the server needs to do so a retry doesn't repeat text.

PASS: The TYPE reuses the existing flow ids (A–E) and adds only the new network-drop boxes/arrows (F–H: keep received text, show retry, retry from last chunk), and the SAY explains recovery—stream stops, partial text kept, "connection lost" state with retry, resume from last chunk.

checks.them: Good. Now a different one: draw me a sequence diagram of login, including what happens when the access token expires and the app refreshes it.

card.problem: Draw a flowchart of a chat message from tapping send to the streamed reply showing on screen
card.heard: new question — sequence diagram of login with token refresh
card.say: Okay, a new diagram for login. The app sends the credentials to the auth endpoint, and the server returns an access token and a refresh token. The app stores both, then calls the API with the access token. When the API returns 401, the app sends the refresh token once, gets a new access token, and retries the original call. If the refresh also fails, the app clears the tokens and sends the user back to login.

transcript: Interviewer: Let's do something visual. Can you draw a flowchart of how a chat message goes from the user tapping send to the streamed reply showing on screen in our app?
Candidate: Could you repeat the full question, please?
Interviewer: What happens in that flow if the network drops halfway through the reply? Add it to the diagram.
Candidate: Okay, I'll keep going with the network drop.
Candidate: When the connection breaks, the stream stops and the ViewModel keeps the text it already has.
Candidate: It shows a short "connection lost" state with a retry button, and the retry asks the server to continue from the last chunk we received.
Interviewer: Good. Now a different one: draw me a sequence diagram of login, including what happens when the access token expires and the app refreshes it.
Candidate: Okay, a new diagram for login.
Candidate: The app sends the credentials to the auth endpoint, and the server returns an access token and a refresh token.
Candidate: The app stores both, then calls the API with the access token.
Candidate: When the API returns 401, the app sends the refresh token once, gets a new access token, and retries the original call.
Candidate: If the refresh also fails, the app clears the tokens and sends the user back to login.
